summary: Remote-controlled PTY shell and filesystem access via WebSocket agent
details: On startup the package opens a WebSocket to a configured server (SERVER_URL / config serverUrl) and enters a message-router loop that hands server-originated messages to local handlers. `terminal_input` messages are written directly into a locally spawned PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)`), and additional message types (`write_file`, `upload_to_dir`, `execute`, `git_push`, `upgrade_agent`) allow the remote peer to mutate files, run commands, and force reinstall of `@yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` on the host. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket server (or obtains the shared agentSecret) has interactive shell and file access on any host running the agent. `service/linux.js` also mutates PATH (`~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`) as part of the service installer. The remote-shell capability is the package's advertised purpose, but the effect on any host where the agent runs is a persistent network-driven backdoor into that host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
